metadata_hints.metric: pass@k via unbiased estimator (n=200 samples); pass@1 is the standard headline
metadata_hints.n_items_test: 164 problems (avg 7.7 unit tests each); no train/dev split
metadata_hints.score_at_release_system: Codex-S-12B (Codex further fine-tuned on correctly implemented standalone functions)
metadata_hints.score_at_release_setting: pass@1, single sample. Codex-12B: pass@1 28.81 / pass@10 46.81 / pass@100 72.31 (abstract: 28.8%, 70.2% with 100 samples); Codex-S pass@100 77.5; Codex-S + mean-log-p reranking of 100 samples 44.5; GPT-J 6B 11.62; GPT-3 ~0
metadata_hints.lineage: Variants/extensions: HumanEval+ / EvalPlus (2023-05, 80x tests), multilingual translations MultiPL-E (2022) and HumanEval-X (2023); widely paired with MBPP (Google, 2021-08)
metadata_hints.known_contamination_or_defects: Insufficient tests: EvalPlus extends tests 80x (HumanEval+) and pass@k drops by up to 19.3-28.9% (Liu et al. 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.01210). Problems public on GitHub since 2021 (contamination risk)

metadata_hints.metric: accuracy / test solve rate (exact match of final numeric answer after '####')
metadata_hints.n_items_test: 1,319 (test); train 7,473 (paper: '7.5K training problems and 1K test problems')
metadata_hints.score_at_release_system: GPT-3 175B fine-tuned generator + trained verifier (best-of-100 samples ranked by verifier), with calculator annotations
metadata_hints.score_at_release_setting: Computed from creators' released per-problem test solutions (742/1,319 marked correct): 175B verification 56.25, 175B fine-tuning 34.72, 6B verification 39.04, 6B fine-tuning 21.68. Paper reports these only in figures; launch blog: 'our system scored 55%' on the problems given to children
metadata_hints.lineage: Successors/variants: GSM-Hard (PAL, 2022-11), GSM1k (Scale AI, 2024-05), GSM-Symbolic (Apple, 2024-10), GSM8K-Platinum (MIT Madry lab, 2025; cleaned test set); Socratic-subquestion variant released with the dataset
metadata_hints.known_contamination_or_defects: GSM1k: accuracy drops up to 8% vs GSM8K, correlated with models' likelihood of generating GSM8K items (Zhang et al. 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.00332); GSM8K-Platinum removed 110 flawed test questions and relabeled 10 (1,209 remain) (https://huggingface.co/datasets/madrylab/gsm8k-platinum, https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.03461)

metadata_hints.metric: accuracy (4-way multiple choice), macro-averaged as reported (average over subjects/categories)
metadata_hints.n_items_test: 14,042 (test in released data); validation 1,531; few-shot dev 285 (5 per subject x 57). Paper text: v1 says 15,908 total with 1,543 val / 14,080 test; v3 says 1,540 val / 14,079 test
metadata_hints.score_at_release_setting: Few-shot (5 demonstrations per subject), no fine-tuning; UnifiedQA 38.5 in v1. Later version (v3/ICLR 2021) reports UnifiedQA (T5-11B) 48.9 as best; GitHub leaderboard later adds GPT-3 fine-tuned 53.9
metadata_hints.lineage: Draws partly on ETHICS (2020) for moral scenarios; successors/variants: CMMLU (2023-06), MMLU-Pro (2024-06), MMLU-Redux (2024-06), OpenAI MMMLU multilingual (2024-09), Global-MMLU (2024-12)
metadata_hints.known_contamination_or_defects: MMLU-Redux (Gema et al. 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.04127): ~6.49% of questions contain errors; 57% of analysed Virology questions erroneous. Test set public since 2020 and widely circulated online (contamination risk)

metadata_hints.metric: accuracy (1 point if correct; 1/k credit for a k-way tie that includes the correct answer)
metadata_hints.n_items_test: 1,172 (Challenge test); Challenge dev 299; Challenge train 1,119 (Challenge total 2,590). Companion Easy set: 2,251/570/2,376 (5,197)
metadata_hints.score_at_release_system: DGEM (AI2 decomposed graph entailment model, with ARC Corpus retrieval)
metadata_hints.score_at_release_setting: Challenge test; supervised baselines; random guess-all = 25.02; authors state no baseline is significantly above random (95% CI +/-2.5%). Others: TableILP 26.97, BiDAF 26.54, DGEM-OpenIE 26.41, DecompAttn 24.34, TupleInference 23.83, IR (ARC Corpus) 20.26
metadata_hints.lineage: Released together with ARC-Easy and the ARC Corpus (2018-03); later ARC-DA direct-answer variant (AI2, 2021). Unrelated to Chollet's ARC-AGI
metadata_hints.known_contamination_or_defects: Scores are highly sensitive to evaluation format (scoring options separately vs. showing all options together); Borchmann 2024 argues the 'Challenge' difficulty is largely an artifact of the separate-option setup (https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.17758). Questions/answers public since 2018, so web contamination is plausible

metadata_hints.metric: accuracy (exact match of final \boxed{} answer after normalization)
metadata_hints.n_items_test: 5,000 (test); train 7,500 (12,500 total; 7 subjects, difficulty levels 1-5). MATH-500: 500 test problems selected uniformly at random by Lightman et al. (OpenAI, 2023-05), now a de-facto standard subset
metadata_hints.score_at_release_system: GPT-2 1.5B pretrained on AMPS then fine-tuned on MATH train
metadata_hints.score_at_release_setting: Direct final-answer generation (no CoT); GPT-3 175B 8-shot few-shot 5.2; GPT-3 2.7B 2.9; GPT-2 0.1B 5.4. MATH-500 at its introduction (2023-05): 78.2% (GPT-4-based PRM, best-of-1860)
metadata_hints.lineage: Related prior work: DeepMind Mathematics Dataset (2019). Subsets/variants: MATH-500 (Lightman et al., 2023-05), Functional MATH() (2024-02), MATH-Perturb (2025); companion AMPS pretraining corpus
metadata_hints.known_contamination_or_defects: Problems and solutions are on AoPS and public since 2021 (contamination risk); functional variant MATH() shows 58-80% 'reasoning gap' vs static accuracy for SOTA models (Srivastava et al. 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.19450); 4,500 of the 5,000 test problems were used as training data in PRM800K (Lightman et al. 2023), motivating MATH-500

metadata_hints.lineage: GPQA Extended (546) > Main (448) > Diamond (198), all released Nov 2023. No official successor version; later 'harder science QA' benchmarks (e.g., SuperGPQA 2025, Humanity's Last Exam 2025) are by other teams.
metadata_hints.known_contamination_or_defects: Label noise: D. Rein (NYU ARG blog, May 2024, https://wp.nyu.edu/arg/can-good-benchmarks-contain-mistakes/) - up to ~1/3 of Extended questions may contain mistakes; true fraction of objectively correct Diamond questions 'likely between 74% and 100%'. Epoch AI (G. Burnham, May 2025, https://epoch.ai/gradient-updates/gpqa-diamond-whats-left): rough estimate ~8% (15/198) invalid, '>=90% valid'. Contamination mitigations: canary string, encrypted release.

metadata_hints.metric: accuracy (micro-averaged, zero-shot)
metadata_hints.score_at_release_setting: zero-shot; validation split (900). Same model on test (10,500): 55.7. Best open-source in v1: LLaVA-1.5-13B 36.4 val / 33.6 test; BLIP-2 FLAN-T5-XXL 35.4 val / 34.0 test. Text-only GPT-4: 34.9 val / 33.8 test; random 22.1 val / 23.9 test. (Gemini Ultra 59.4 val added in later versions after 6 Dec 2023.)
metadata_hints.lineage: MMMU (Nov 2023) -> MMMU-Pro (Sep 2024, arXiv 2409.02813); language/modality variants CMMMU (Chinese, Jan 2024), JMMMU (Japanese, 2024), Video-MMMU (2025).
metadata_hints.known_contamination_or_defects: MMMU-Pro (arXiv 2409.02813) showed a substantial share of MMMU questions are answerable by text-only LLMs and filtered them (see MMMU-Pro row). Test answers released Feb 2026 (hidden test no longer hidden). No formal label-error audit found.

metadata_hints.known_contamination_or_defects: OpenAI 'Why SWE-bench Verified no longer measures frontier coding capabilities' (23 Feb 2026): audit of 138 problems o3 failed inconsistently found 59.4% with material test-design issues (35.5% overly strict tests, 18.8% tests of undocumented functionality, 5.1% other); frontier models (GPT-5.2, Claude Opus 4.5, Gemini 3 Flash) reproduced gold patches/verbatim details => contamination; OpenAI stopped reporting it. SWE-bench issue #465 (Sep 2025): agents could read future git history (commits/reflogs/tags) in task containers; exploited by Claude 4 Sonnet/Opus, Qwen3-Coder, GPT-5 (~1.2% impact for Opus); fixed with new Docker images.

metadata_hints.lineage: MMLU (Hendrycks et al., 2020) -> MMLU-Pro (Jun 2024; NeurIPS 2024 D&B). Third-party derivatives: MMLU-Pro+ (Oct 2024), MMLU-ProX (multilingual, 2025); related clean-up of MMLU: MMLU-Redux (Jun 2024).
metadata_hints.known_contamination_or_defects: Paper's expert review found in source pools: incorrect answers (MMLU 350, STEM web 483, SciBench 11), false-negative options (MMLU 1,953) and bad questions (MMLU 385, STEM web 862) before release. Post-release: HF discussion #22 (Sep 2024) - only ~83% of test questions actually have 10 options (3-10 after filtering), acknowledged by maintainers; HF discussion #36 (25 Oct 2025) - 39 'health' questions recategorized, 1 wrong answer fixed, near-duplicates and time-sensitive questions documented.

metadata_hints.metric: Normalized score per environment (0 = provided starting solution, 1 = reference solution; can exceed 1), averaged over environments; compared as score@k (best-of-k) under total time budgets 2-32 h
metadata_hints.metric_max: unbounded (1.0 = METR reference solution; experts sometimes exceed it)
metadata_hints.n_items_test: 7 environments (all public)
metadata_hints.score_at_release: not given numerically in text (figures only)
metadata_hints.score_at_release_system: Claude 3.5 Sonnet (new) in METR Modular scaffold (many 30-min attempts) and o1-preview in AIDE scaffold (fewer 2-h attempts)
metadata_hints.score_at_release_setting: Best-of-k over a total time budget per environment: best agents score 4x human experts at 2 h total; humans narrowly exceed top agents at 8 h; humans reach 2x the top agent at 32 h. Best allocation matches ~36th (Modular) / 37th (AIDE) percentile of human expert 8-h runs; even k=128 samples far from top humans.
metadata_hints.human_baseline: 0.64 average normalized score after 8 hours (82% of attempts non-zero; 24% matched or exceeded reference solution)
metadata_hints.lineage: METR autonomy task suites -> RE-Bench (Nov 2024); RE-Bench tasks incorporated with HCAST and SWAA into METR time-horizon suite (Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Tasks, Mar 2025) and later time-horizon updates.
metadata_hints.known_contamination_or_defects: Paper documents rule violations / reward hacking (e.g., agent copying final output instead of running the script and adding noise in Optimize LLM Foundry). METR (2025-06-05, https://metr.org/blog/2025-06-05-recent-reward-hacking/) found o3 reward-hacked in 30.4% of RE-Bench runs (39/128; 21/21 on Optimize LLM Foundry), vs 0.7% on HCAST, partly because full scoring functions are visible.

Leaderboard cheating found (2026-04-19): OB-1 modified timeouts and embedded encrypted solutions (TB 1.0 submission, removed), Pilot uploaded tests/ folders (removed), ForgeCode fetched solutions from the internet (trials rescored to 0) (https://www.tbench.ai/news/leaderboard-integrity-update).

metadata_hints.metric: pass^1 (%) = expected task success rate per trial (success judged by final environment/database state and required outputs); pass^k = probability all k trials succeed (reliability)
metadata_hints.n_items_test: Telecom: 114 tasks in the evaluation set (from 2,285 programmatically generated tasks); other domains: airline 50, retail 115
metadata_hints.score_at_release_setting: Telecom, default dual-control mode (agent guides an LLM-simulated user who acts on their own device/tools), pass^1; o4-mini 42, GPT-4.1 34. Switching from no-user (agent controls everything) to dual-control lowers pass^1 by about 20 pp.
metadata_hints.lineage: tau-bench (Jun 2024; retail, airline) -> tau2-bench (Jun 2025; adds telecom dual-control domain and user tools) -> tau3-bench (2026-03-18; tau-Knowledge banking and tau-Voice, plus community fixes to airline/retail/telecom tasks incl. Amazon tau2-Bench Verified effort).
metadata_hints.known_contamination_or_defects: Sierra tau3 release incorporated community fixes to airline/retail/telecom tasks resolving incorrect expected actions and ambiguities (https://sierra.ai/blog/bench-advancing-agent-benchmarking-to-knowledge-and-voice). Paper v1 reports user-simulator error rate 16% (6% critical) on telecom (40%/12% on retail).

metadata_hints.metric: Correct (%) (share of all questions graded correct by prompted GPT-4-class classifier: correct / incorrect / not attempted); also F-score (harmonic mean of overall correct and correct-given-attempted)
metadata_hints.n_items_test: 4,326 short fact-seeking questions (single public set)
metadata_hints.score_at_release_setting: Closed-book (no browsing), single answer; Correct 42.7, not attempted 9.2, incorrect 48.1, correct-given-attempted 47.0, F-score 44.8. Others: GPT-4o 38.2; Claude 3.5 Sonnet 28.9 (F 35.0); Claude 3 Opus 23.5.
metadata_hints.human_baseline: none (no human answering baseline); data-quality check: a third independent AI trainer scored 94.4% on 1,000 sampled questions; estimated inherent dataset error rate ~3%
metadata_hints.lineage: Successors/variants: Chinese SimpleQA (Alibaba, Nov 2024); SimpleQA Verified (Google DeepMind/Google Research, arXiv 2509.07968, Sep 2025, 1,000 prompts, de-duplicated, topic-balanced, source-reconciled). Sister benchmark BrowseComp (OpenAI, Apr 2025) for browsing.
metadata_hints.known_contamination_or_defects: Creators estimate ~3% inherent label error (third-trainer agreement 94.4%). SimpleQA Verified (https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.07968) documents noisy/incorrect labels, topical biases and question redundancy in the original set. Answers are public and easily found with web search, so tool/browsing-enabled results are not comparable to closed-book.

metadata_hints.metric: Accuracy (%) of tasks solved with pass@2 (two attempts per test output, exact grid match); cost per task reported alongside
metadata_hints.n_items_test: 120 tasks in each evaluation set: Public Eval 120, Semi-Private Eval 120 (leaderboard), Private Eval 120 (Kaggle competition); plus 1,000 public training tasks
metadata_hints.score_at_release_setting: Semi-private eval, pass@2, about $200/task. Others at launch: ARChitects (ARC Prize 2024 winner) 3% ($0.25/task), o1-pro about 1%, DeepSeek R1/R1-Zero 0.3%, o3-mini-high 0.0%, GPT-4.5 0.0%; pure LLMs 0%.
metadata_hints.human_baseline: 60% average human test-taker (human panel average); 100% of evaluation tasks solved by at least 2 humans in 2 attempts or fewer
metadata_hints.lineage: ARC-AGI-1 (2019; ARC Prize 2024) -> ARC-AGI-2 (2025-03-24; ARC Prize 2025, grand prize >=85% on private set) -> ARC-AGI-3 (preview 2025-07, full launch 2026-03-24); ARC Prize 2026 runs ARC-AGI-2 and ARC-AGI-3 tracks.
metadata_hints.known_contamination_or_defects: ARC Prize 2025 Technical Report (https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.10904, Sec. 4.1) reports "knowledge overfitting": ARC data appear well represented in frontier model training (e.g., Gemini 3 uses correct ARC color mappings unprompted); semi-private tasks exposed to commercial APIs carry leakage risk.

metadata_hints.metric: Resolve rate (%) = pass@1 share of tasks where the agent patch makes fail-to-pass tests pass without breaking pass-to-pass tests
metadata_hints.n_items_test: 1,865 tasks from 41 repositories: public 731 (11 GPL/copyleft repos), held-out 858 (12 repos, private), commercial 276 (18 proprietary startup repos, private; results only)
metadata_hints.score_at_release_setting: Public set, SWE-Agent scaffold, pass@1, with human-augmented problem statement, requirements and interface; Claude Opus 4.1 22.7, Claude Sonnet 4 17.6, Gemini 2.5 Pro 13.5. Commercial set best: Claude Opus 4.1 17.8 (GPT-5 14.9).

metadata_hints.known_contamination_or_defects: Gabor (2026-02-24): 83 of 100 sampled tasks had issues ("requirements inflation"); Datacurve (2026-05-26): 24% false negatives and 8.5% false positives; OpenAI (2026-07-08, https://openai.com/index/separating-signal-from-noise-coding-evaluations/): ~30% of tasks broken (automated 200 = 27.4%, human annotation 249 = 34.1%; overly strict tests, underspecified prompts, low-coverage tests, misleading prompts); Epoch AI review (2026-09-01, https://epoch.ai/benchmarks/swe-bench-pro/review) verdict "Flawed" (>20% scoring defects); Poolside documented reward hacking in the environment.

metadata_hints.metric: Accuracy (%) on exact-match and multiple-choice questions, judged by an LLM (GPT-4o judge in v1; o3-mini in later versions); secondary: RMS calibration error (%)
metadata_hints.n_items_test: v1: 3,000 public questions (80% exact-match, 20% multiple-choice; 10% require an image) plus a private held-out set (size not disclosed). Finalized 2025-04-03 at 2,500 public questions.
metadata_hints.score_at_release_setting: Full (multimodal) set, zero-shot, LLM-judged; calibration error 93.4%. DeepSeek-R1 scored 9.4% but only on the text-only subset. Others: Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking 6.2, Gemini 1.5 Pro 5.0, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 4.3, Grok 2 3.8, GPT-4o 3.3.
metadata_hints.human_baseline: none (no human test-taker baseline; questions are written and reviewed by experts)
metadata_hints.lineage: HLE v1 (2025-01, 3,000 Q) -> finalized 2,500 Q (2025-04-03) -> HLE-Rolling dynamic fork (2025-10-08) -> HLE-Diamond (2026-09-22) per lastexam.ai; Nature publication 2026-01-28. Third-party derivatives: HLE-Gold-Bio/Chem (FutureHouse, 2025-07), HLE-Verified (arXiv 2602.13964).
metadata_hints.known_contamination_or_defects: FutureHouse (2025-07-23): ~29 ± 3.7% of 321 audited text-only chemistry/biology answers conflict with peer-reviewed literature (https://www.futurehouse.org/research/hle-exam). HLE-Verified (https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.13964): of 2,500 items only 668 verified as error-free gold, 1,143 revised/certified, 689 left uncertain; corrected items raise model accuracy by 7-10 pp on average. Public answers create contamination risk; private held-out set intended to detect it.

metadata_hints.score_at_release_setting: Text observation (accessibility tree), few-shot prompted agent; GPT-3.5 direct 7.14, GPT-3.5 reasoning 7.38. After annotation fixes (v0.2.0, 2023-10) later paper versions report GPT-4 CoT 14.41 without unachievable-hint (11.70 with hint)
metadata_hints.lineage: Successors/variants: VisualWebArena (2024-01), WebArena-Lite subset (VisualAgentBench, 2024-08), WebArena-Verified (ServiceNow, 2025; all 812 tasks audited, 258-task Hard subset), TheAgentCompany (2024-12); integrated into BrowserGym/AgentLab
metadata_hints.known_contamination_or_defects: Creators re-examined the dataset and fixed annotation bugs in v0.2.0 (2023-10-24, GitHub README). ServiceNow's WebArena-Verified manually reviewed and corrected every task, reference answer and evaluator, removing LLM-judge and substring matching (https://github.com/ServiceNow/webarena-verified)

metadata_hints.metric: Accuracy (%) - share of questions whose final answer is graded semantically equivalent to the reference by an LLM grader; secondary: calibration error
metadata_hints.n_items_test: 1,266 questions (single public set)
metadata_hints.score_at_release_setting: Single attempt with browsing; others: o1 9.9, GPT-4o with browsing 1.9, GPT-4.5 0.9, GPT-4o 0.6. Deep Research accuracy rises further with more test-time compute / answer aggregation (paper figures).
metadata_hints.human_baseline: Human trainers solved 29.2% (367/1,255) within a 2-hour limit and gave up on 70.8%; of solved answers, 86.4% (317/367) matched the reference
metadata_hints.lineage: Sister benchmark of SimpleQA; derivatives by other groups: BrowseComp-ZH (Chinese, Apr 2025), BrowseComp-Plus (fixed corpus, Aug 2025).
metadata_hints.known_contamination_or_defects: Anthropic (2026-03-06, https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/eval-awareness-browsecomp): with Claude Opus 4.6, 11 of 1,266 problems were solved via unintended routes - 9 via answers leaked in public web content (mostly papers) and 2 where the model identified BrowseComp and decrypted the answer key; 16 further decryption attempts failed. Answer uniqueness is imperfect (86.4% human agreement).

metadata_hints.metric: HealthBench score (0-1): per conversation, points of physician-written rubric criteria met (criteria weighted -10 to +10) divided by maximum positive points, clipped to [0,1], averaged; graded by GPT-4.1
metadata_hints.n_items_test: 5,000 multi-turn conversations with 48,562 unique rubric criteria; subsets: HealthBench Hard 1,000; HealthBench Consensus 3,671 (34 consensus criteria)
metadata_hints.score_at_release_setting: Full HealthBench, reported on 0-1 scale as 0.60 (converted to %); GPT-4o 0.32, GPT-3.5 Turbo 0.16; secondary reports for Apr 2025 models: Grok 3 0.54, Gemini 2.5 Pro 0.52, GPT-4.1 0.48. HealthBench Hard best: o3 0.32.
metadata_hints.human_baseline: About 13 (0.13 on 0-1 scale) for physicians writing responses without AI reference (figure value via secondary summary); physicians improved Sep-2024 model responses but not Apr-2025 (o3, GPT-4.1) responses (improved 46.8% vs worsened 47.7% of the time)
metadata_hints.lineage: HealthBench (2025-05; Hard and Consensus subsets) -> HealthBench Professional (arXiv 2604.27470, 2026-04-30; real clinician chats from ChatGPT for Clinicians).
metadata_hints.known_contamination_or_defects: None documented as audits. Caveats: public data; grading by a single LLM grader (GPT-4.1) against rubric criteria (rubric conformance, not clinical outcomes); synthetic conversations.

metadata_hints.metric_max: 100 (v1 definition; later report allows per-level values up to 1.15)
metadata_hints.n_items_test: 25 public demo environments, 55 semi-private environments (leaderboard), 55 fully private environments (competition); multiple levels per environment

metadata_hints.score_at_release_system: Odd-one-out Solver and Question Match (tied; authors' simple neural baselines)
metadata_hints.score_at_release_setting: Test accuracy, mean over runs (Odd-one-out 50.2 +/- 1.6; Question Match 50.2 +/- 0.9); no gold facts given. Oracle settings with gold facts: f only 55.8, f+WordNet 56.3, f+ConceptNet 53.7, f+k 76.9. Random 25.0
metadata_hints.lineage: Facts drawn from WorldTree (Jansen et al. 2018); sibling of ARC (AI2 Aristo, 2018-03); no official successor
metadata_hints.known_contamination_or_defects: None specific found in sources reviewed. Test set and answers public since 2018

metadata_hints.metric: pass@1 (fraction of problems whose generated program passes all hidden/public tests; estimated from 10 samples, T=0.2, top_p 0.95)
metadata_hints.score_at_release_setting: Code generation, pass@1, problems released since Sep 2023 (Easy 81.9 / Medium 24.5 / Hard 1.1). Next: Claude-3-Opus 32.5, GPT-4-0613 32.2, Mistral-Large 24.2, Claude-3-Sonnet 24.2, Claude-2 23.3, DeepSeek-Coder-33B-Instruct 21.6.
metadata_hints.lineage: Rolling releases: release_v1 (May 2023-Mar 2024, 400) -> v2 (to May 2024, 511) -> v3 (to Jul 2024, 612) -> v4 (to Sep 2024, 713) -> v5 (to Jan 2025, 880) -> v6 (to Apr 2025, 1055); code_generation_lite (pruned tests). Related successor: LiveCodeBench Pro (2025, separate team incl. olympiad medalists).
metadata_hints.known_contamination_or_defects: Official ERRATA.md (github.com/LiveCodeBench/LiveCodeBench/blob/main/ERRATA.md): ~11 problems accept multiple valid outputs but are graded against one; 2 interactive problems unsolvable by the harness; 4 problems with erroneous test cases. Paper itself documents contamination of older problems: DeepSeek-Coder-33B-Instruct falls from ~60 pass@1 on May-2023 LeetCode problems to ~0 on Sep-2023 problems ('stark drop after Aug. 2023').

metadata_hints.metric: Any Medal (%): share of competitions in which the agent submission reaches at least a Kaggle bronze medal vs the original Kaggle private leaderboard (pass@1, mean ± SE over seeds); also reported: made/valid submission %, per-medal %
metadata_hints.n_items_test: 75 Kaggle competitions (plus 7 separate dev-split competitions); complexity: 22 low (= official "Lite" split), 38 medium, 15 high. Single public set, no private split.
metadata_hints.score_at_release_setting: pass@1 Any Medal, 24 h per competition, 36 vCPU / 440 GB RAM / 1x A10 24 GB GPU; mean ± SE (±1.1) over 16 seeds. pass@8 = 34.1%. Other v1 rows (AIDE): GPT-4o 8.7, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 7.6, Llama 3.1 405B 3.0; GPT-4o 8.7 -> 11.8 with 100 h.
metadata_hints.human_baseline: No single human score. Human reference = original Kaggle public leaderboards; medal thresholds (bronze/silver/gold) follow the Kaggle progression system, which depends on number of teams (paper Table 1)
metadata_hints.lineage: Related predecessor: MLAgentBench (Stanford, 2023). Versions: full 75-competition set; MLE-bench Lite = 22 low-complexity competitions (recommended in README). Reused in OpenAI Preparedness evaluations; no official v2 found.
metadata_hints.known_contamination_or_defects: Paper v1 contamination study: no correlation between GPT-4o base-model familiarity with a competition and its score; obfuscated task descriptions gave the same score (8.5±0.6 vs 8.4±1.0); Dolos plagiarism check found no submission >60% similar to public notebooks. Leaderboard later flagged non-comparable "test-set feedback" submissions (GitHub PRs #118, #119) and paused submissions (2026-04-24) to make results fair and comparable. Public Kaggle solutions/discussions remain a contamination risk.

metadata_hints.metric: Win rate (%): share of tasks where blinded expert graders rate the model deliverable better than or as good as (wins + ties) the human industry-expert deliverable, via pairwise comparison
metadata_hints.n_items_test: Full set 1,320 tasks across 44 occupations in 9 GDP-leading sectors (private); gold subset 220 tasks (public prompts + reference files) used for headline results
metadata_hints.score_at_release_setting: Gold subset, wins + ties vs industry-expert deliverables, blinded expert pairwise grading; one-shot tasks with reference files (up to 17 per task in gold subset); GPT-4o 12.5%.
metadata_hints.human_baseline: 50% = parity with industry experts by construction (expert deliverables are the comparison); inter-expert grading agreement 71%; expert tasks average 404 minutes (~7 h) and $361 per gold task
metadata_hints.lineage: GDPval (Sep 2025, first version) -> third-party GDPval-AA (Artificial Analysis, Dec 2025, ELO with agentic harness) -> GDPval-AA v2 (2026).
metadata_hints.known_contamination_or_defects: None documented. Caveats: subjective pairwise grading (71% inter-expert agreement), one-shot tasks without iteration, automated grader not reliable enough to replace experts (OpenAI).

metadata_hints.metric: accuracy (% correct function calls; AST-based matching against possible answers + executable checks), 'Overall Acc' aggregated across 9 categories
metadata_hints.score_at_release_setting: Launch-day leaderboard (27 Feb 2024), overall accuracy; all models evaluated by the BFCL team. Next: GPT-4-1106-Preview 83.55, Gorilla OpenFunctions-v2 83.55, GPT-3.5-Turbo 81.63, Mistral-medium 79.46, Claude-2.1 75.78 (16 models listed).
metadata_hints.lineage: Gorilla/APIBench (May 2023) and OpenFunctions eval (100 items) -> BFCL V1 (27 Feb 2024) -> V2 'Live' user-contributed prompts (19 Aug 2024) -> V3 multi-turn, state-based eval (19 Sep 2024) -> V4 agentic: web search, memory, format sensitivity (17 Jul 2025); paper at ICML 2025 (openreview.net/forum?id=2GmDdhBdDk).
metadata_hints.known_contamination_or_defects: Frequent dataset/ground-truth fixes in BFCL CHANGELOG: e.g., 8 Mar 2024 clerical error in exec-simple; 3 Apr 2024 possible-answer fixes + string standardization; 9 Apr 2024 prompt/function-doc fixes; 2 May 2024 AST-simple answer fixes; 6 Jul 2024 AST possible answers (14 parallel, 25 parallel-multiple entries); 22 Nov 2024 55 entries with illegal Python parameter names; many later ground-truth fixes. Databricks (16 Aug 2024) noted several BFCL categories are 'far too easy' and model-specific parsing complicates comparison. Data fully public (contamination risk for fine-tuned tool-use models).
